note_add: Tax: Connecticut DRS rules that renting a campsite is renting real property, so no room occupancy or sales tax is charged on it, hookups and RVs included; cabins carry the 15% room occupancy tax. The site fee covers six people including children, the most a site takes, except that a registrant's own children under 18 may all stay for the basic fee. Two motor vehicles a site; overnight parking for more is not available. Whether a camper's out-of-state vehicle pays the day-use parking fee is not published (CT plates park free; out-of-state $6-22 a day at fee parks). No weekend or holiday rate was found.

sources.quote: There is a $9.00 fee for making each reservation.

Rental of a campsite is the rental of real property, which is not subject to either the room occupancy tax or sales and use taxes, regardless of whether the campsite has electricity or sewer hookups and whether the customer parks a recreational vehicle on the campsite.
The campsite fee covers six (6) persons, including children.

The maximum number of occupants allowed per campsite is six. However, a parent or parents accompanied by any number of their children under the age of eighteen may occupy a single campsite irrespective of the six person limitation.
No more than two motor vehicles are permitted on a single campsite, unless otherwise noted.
Daily parking rates apply for visitors arriving in out-of-state registered vehicles.

unsettled.entrance: CT-registered vehicles park free everywhere; out-of-state vehicles pay day-use parking at fee parks ($6-22/day, Hammonasset $15 weekday / $22 weekend). No page says whether a registered camper's out-of-state vehicle pays it; ctparks says visitors in out-of-state vehicles do.
unsettled.extra_vehicle.amount: Two vehicles a site; no page says whether the second is free or charged.
unsettled.nonresident: Each entry carries its own resident / non-resident pair; the differential varies ($10 at most parks, $12 at Salt Rock), so no row-wide figure.
unsettled.surcharges.weekend/holiday: None found, but CT publishes no complete camping fee schedule (the RCSA camping rules carry no fee table), so no zero.

summary: CT: $9 reservation fee confirmed; no tax on campsites (DRS PS 2017(2)); fee covers 6 people, the site maximum (own children exempt); 2 vehicles max; camper parking for out-of-state plates unsettled.

note_add: The daily rate covers six people and one vehicle pass (the drivable camping unit or the vehicle towing it); a second car pass is $12 a reservation, two vehicles a site at most. Visitor passes are $8 a vehicle a day, at most two at a time. Walk-ins pay no reservation fee. Tax: the Division of Taxation rules that sites where campers bring their own tent or RV carry neither sales nor hotel tax; cabins supplied by the campground carry 7% sales tax plus 6% hotel tax. The rate table has one rate a night, no weekend or holiday premium.

The camping daily rate covers six (6) persons per campsite and one vehicle pass which would include a drivable camping unit or a vehicle towing a camping unit.

summary: RI: rate covers 6 people (the site cap) and one vehicle (so no entry charge); 2nd car $12 per reservation, 2 max; no tax on own-RV sites (RI Notice 2025-04); one nightly rate, no weekend/holiday premium; $8.75 reservation fee confirmed.

note_add: The Commonwealth's fee regulation (801 CMR 4.02) prices DCR camping per site per day and lists no extra-person or extra-vehicle charge, nor any weekend or holiday rate; its only parking row under camping is day-visitor parking ($8 a vehicle a day). Most campgrounds allow 2 vehicles and 4 adults (or 2 adults and the children in their care) a site; Scusset RV sites take one camping vehicle only. The regulation's inland non-resident figure ($55) is a dollar above the current fee page's $54. Tax: no source states whether the room occupancy excise applies to a DCR campsite.

unsettled.entrance: Registered campers pay no gate fee for camping, but DCR charges day-use parking at the same parks ($8 MA / $30 non-MA at most, $14 / $40 at Horseneck, Salisbury and Scusset, May 23 - Oct 12) and no source says whether a camper's vehicle is exempt. mass.gov blocks automated fetch; searches of it found no camper exemption.
unsettled.tax: No mass.gov or DOR source addresses a campsite; 830 CMR 64G.1.1 exempts 'lodging accommodations at a federal, state or municipal institution' and taxes rooms, which reads as no tax on a state campsite but is not stated, so no zero.
unsettled.reservation_fee: Kept at $4.50; mass.gov's camping-fees page (blocked to fetch) is reported by search to say '$4.50 transaction charge per reservation, non-refundable' - not re-read directly, value unchanged.

summary: MA: 801 CMR 4.02 fee schedule shows no extra-person or extra-vehicle charge and no weekend/holiday rate (2 vehicles a site, read via search since mass.gov blocks fetch); entrance (camper day-use parking) and tax remain unsettled.

note_add: Registered campers use the park's day-use areas free until closing on check-out day; their visitors pay day-use admission. Tax: the Vermont Department of Taxes treats bare land for a customer's tent or RV as not a sleeping accommodation, so tent and RV sites carry no rooms tax; lean-tos, cabins and cottages are priced including the 9% meals and rooms tax. The 2022 fee rule makes children 3 and under free and allows two vehicles a site with no vehicle charge; it sets one nightly rate (prime sites +$2), no weekend or holiday rate.

sources.quote: Registered campers can use day use areas at no charge. A camper receipt allows the holders to use day use areas until normal closing hour on the scheduled day of check out.
Bare land for customer-provided tents or recreational vehicles, as well as tent platforms, are not sleeping accommodations.
Rentals of sleeping accommodations are subject to rooms tax.
Vermont Residents = $30.00 per night including VT Meals and Rooms Tax
Base site price is for up to 4 people.
Extra People Over 4 (max 8) $8 per person, per night
There is no charge for children 3 years and under for camping.
The maximum number of vehicles allowed per site, including self-propelled sleeping units, shall be two.

unsettled.extra_person.child: The 2022 rule makes children 3 and under free, but the July 2025 price update and fees page don't repeat it, so it stays in the note rather than as child: 0.

summary: VT: extra_person (4 included, $8, max 8) verified; campers' day use free (entrance 0); no rooms tax on tent/RV sites (lean-tos include it); 2 vehicles, no vehicle fee in the fee rule; no weekend/holiday rate.

note_add: At most four adults and six people a site, except in designated areas; at RV-only campgrounds no more than the RV sleeps. Tax: New Hampshire took campsites out of the meals and rooms tax in 2010; cabins and yurts are still taxed. Visitors register and pay the day-use fee.

sources.quote: Reservation fee is $7.00.
AN ACT eliminating the meals and rooms tax on campsites.

Rates cover two adults and up to four children on the site. The maximum number of adults allowed per site is four, with a maximum of six people total, except in designated areas. Each additional adult is charged $10 per night, and each additional child is charged $5 per night.
At RV-only campgrounds, the maximum number of persons registered to a campsite shall not exceed the number of persons the recreational vehicle is designed to sleep.
Visitors are permitted and must register with the campground and pay the day use fee.

unsettled.extra_vehicle: No vehicle limit or extra-vehicle fee is published on the rates or policy pages or in Res 7300.
unsettled.nonresident: No non-resident camping rate appears, but no complete fee schedule is published, so no zero.
unsettled.surcharges.weekend/holiday: None published; no complete schedule to rest a zero on.

summary: NH: $7 reservation fee and extra-person terms verified, max 6 people added; campsites exempt from meals and rooms tax since 2010 (HB 1445); entrance, extra vehicles and weekend/holiday unsettled.

note_add: The camping fee includes the park's day-use fee; visitors pay day use or show a season pass. Site fees are for parties of six or fewer, and a larger party must book a group site. The 9% lodging tax is charged on all camping fees. The $5 reservation fee is per site per night, so the reservation_fee figure understates a multi-night booking.
